title: The CAP theorem
researchPrompt: Explain what a distributed system must give up during a network partition, and why the popular pick-two summary is misleading.
suggestedAngles: Start from the partition as the thing you do not get to choose
Reframe it as a choice between consistency and availability only while partitioned
Use a concrete two-datacentre example rather than the abstract triangle

title: How public-key cryptography lets strangers share a secret
researchPrompt: Explain how two parties who have never met can establish a shared secret over a channel an eavesdropper is fully reading.
suggestedAngles: Use the paint-mixing analogy, then say precisely where the analogy breaks
Build on one-way functions: easy forwards, hard backwards
Separate key exchange from encryption from signing

references.label: Diffie & Hellman (1976) — New Directions in Cryptography

title: Byzantine fault tolerance
researchPrompt: Explain why agreement among distributed nodes gets dramatically harder when a node may lie rather than merely fail, and where the two-thirds threshold comes from.
suggestedAngles: Contrast crash faults with arbitrary faults as failure models
Derive the 3f+1 bound from the impossibility of distinguishing the liar
Connect it to a real system: consensus protocols or blockchains

references.label: Lamport, Shostak & Pease (1982) — The Byzantine Generals Problem
